title: Factory Planning Card (RFC-0019 section 3.1)
description: One card on the CFactory planning board: the human-owned, editable unit of PLANNED work, served over `/api/cards`. A card is deliberately NOT a `work_items` row. `work_items` is a correlation store that CFactory reconciles and prunes from upstream completion events; a card carries fields no upstream event knows about (title, acceptance criteria, priority, milestone, assignee) and a reconcile would overwrite or drop them. The two live in separate tables and `correlation_key` is the join: NULL while the card is planned, set once the card enters the factory. This schema describes the card RESOURCE as served; `$defs.card_create` and `$defs.card_patch` describe the request bodies, and `$defs.card_list` the list response. Companion document: apis/planning-card.md.

card.description: The card resource as served by GET /api/cards/{card_key}. Every field is always present: the nullable ones carry an explicit null rather than being omitted, so a consumer never has to distinguish `not set` from `not sent by this version of the server`.

created_at.description: When the card was created. Server-owned: set on POST and never mutable thereafter.

updated_at.description: When any field last changed. Server-owned: rewritten on every accepted mutation, including one made by a factory runtime writing status back.

card_key.description: Stable, human-quotable id, e.g. `FCT-42`. Server-assigned from a per-tenant sequence and IMMUTABLE once issued - it is the path segment of every single-card route, so a rename would break every link a human or an agent has kept. Not the correlation key: see `correlation_key`.

tenant_id.description: Which tenant owns this card. Present in the resource so a consumer can assert what it is reading, but NEVER accepted from a request body: the server derives it from the calling credential (`CFACTORY_API_KEYS` / `CFACTORY_MULTI_TENANT`). Accepting it from the body would make cross-tenant writes a matter of typing a different string.

title.description: One line: what is to be done. Human-owned - no upstream event ever rewrites it.

acceptance_criteria.description: What `done` means, one testable statement per entry. Human-owned. When the card dispatches (RFC-0019 section 3.2) these become the acceptance criteria of the RFC-0002 task contract, which is why an empty list is allowed while planning but a card dispatched without any gives the factory nothing to verify against.

status.description: Board column. `ready` is the dispatch trigger: a `ready` card WITH a `tier` is a first-class intake source alongside a labelled GitHub issue (RFC-0019 section 3.2). This vocabulary is the card's own and MUST NOT be classified through apis/status-taxonomy.json, which exists to normalise the four services' RUNTIME statuses: `ready` is a `done` token there and `blocked` is a `failed` token, so a card waiting to be picked up would read as finished and a card a human parked would read as a failure.

priority.description: Backlog order, LOWER IS HIGHER priority (0 is the top of the board). An integer rather than an enum so a card can be inserted between two others without renumbering the column. Ties are legal; the server orders by (priority ASC, created_at ASC, card_key ASC) so a list is stable across requests. Defaults to 100 when omitted on create, leaving room to insert above and below.

tier.description: RFC-0011 difficulty tier, the same vocabulary as the `factory:low|medium|hard` labels and the task contract's `execution.autonomy_tier`. Note `hard`, not `high`. NULL means not yet classified: the card is still a plan. The tier drives model, planning depth, human gate, VAL floor and merge behaviour once the card dispatches, so a `ready` card with a NULL tier is not dispatched - it stays on the board waiting for a human or an agent to classify it.

assignee.description: Who is on it: a human handle, or a factory runtime (`pfactory` / `aifactory` / `tfactory` / `cfactory`) once the card is in flight. Free-form because the board must be able to name a person who has no account here. NULL is unassigned.

milestone.description: Milestone name this card belongs to, free-form. Deliberately a string and not a foreign key: the roadmap view groups by it, and RFC-0019 section 3.5 keeps GitHub authoritative, so this holds the GitHub milestone TITLE once card-to-issue mirroring lands (phase 6). NULL is unscheduled.

correlation_key.description: RFC-0001 correlation key: the GitHub issue number as a string, or a synthetic <prefix>-<id>. THE JOIN between this card and the `work_items` timeline, and the reason the two are separate tables. NULL for as long as the card is only planned; set exactly once, when the card enters the factory. Write-once: a server MUST reject an attempt to point an already-joined card at a different key (a card is one unit of work, and re-pointing it would silently reattribute its history).

card_create.description: POST /api/cards request body. Only human-owned planning fields are settable. `card_key`, `tenant_id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` are server-owned, and `correlation_key` is set later by whatever dispatches the card - so none of them are accepted here and `additionalProperties: false` makes sending one an error rather than a silently ignored field.

card_patch.description: PATCH /api/cards/{card_key} request body: a partial card. Every mutable field may be sent, including `status` (move) and `priority` (reprioritise) - one route covers both, so an agent needs no special-case endpoints to do what a human does by dragging. Sending no field at all is a mistake, not a no-op, hence `minProperties: 1`.

card_list.description: GET /api/cards response. An envelope rather than a bare array so pagination and echoed filters can be added additively later without breaking every consumer; `total` is the number of cards matching the filter, which equals `len(cards)` while there is no pagination.

cards.description: Cards for the calling tenant only, ordered by (priority ASC, created_at ASC, card_key ASC).
